election._note: Elected 24 April 2022 for a four-year term, so the next is due by spring 2026 -- early in the game's clock; no fixed date announced. Quota allocation in 11 constituencies with 8 national levelling seats, which the machinery's largest-remainder pr_national reads the nearest; the statutory threshold is the national 4%. Wikipedia, 'Next Slovenian parliamentary election'.

dissolution._note: Art. 111: after consultations the President proposes a candidate Prime Minister; if the Assembly fails to elect one within 50 days of the first proposal, the President may dissolve it and call elections -- the president-with-limits shape the rule's name reads, the poll landing roughly six weeks after the call, notice_months 1. Ustava RS, Art. 111.

head_of_state._note: The President, popularly elected for five years; last elected November 2022, so the next is due autumn 2027. Mostly ceremonial, with the formation proposal and the dissolution role above. Wikipedia, 'President of Slovenia'.
head_of_state.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 168: a proposal may come from twenty deputies, the Government or thirty thousand voters; Art. 169: adopted by a two-thirds majority of ALL deputies. Ustava RS, Arts. 168-169.
amendment._referendum_note: Art. 170: the Assembly must call a referendum on the ENTRY INTO FORCE of a constitutional amendment if thirty deputies demand it within seven days of adoption -- a post-adoption gate, which the machinery's optional reads. Ustava RS, Art. 170.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Arts. 168-170 set only the two-thirds bar and the thirty-deputy referendum; the Constitution carries no eternity clause protecting the form of the state, so this reads true -- GBR's shape with a thinner citation, the way AUT's note flags its own row.

judicial._note: Ustavno sodišče: decides on the conformity of laws with the Constitution, and reviews a priori on the request of the President or the Government. Ustava RS, Art. 160.

formation._note: Art. 111: the President proposes a candidate Prime Minister after consulting the parliamentary groups, and the Assembly ELECTS the Prime Minister by a majority of all deputies, the President then appointing the ministers on the PM's proposal (Art. 112) -- the Assembly's election of the PM is the machinery's investiture. Art. 116 is the censure half: a no-confidence vote must NAME a candidate successor, who takes office when a majority of ALL deputies vote for him or her -- Slovenia's constructive vote of no confidence, the same shape Germany's Grundgesetz Art. 67 gives the rule its name. Ustava RS, Arts. 111-112 and 116.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2024-2025, rounded, on the same conventions as SVK.json's block. VAT 22% is the statutory standard rate; corporate 19% is the statutory rate, reduced from 22% in 2020; income 25 is a blend of the progressive 16-50% schedule; capital gains 25% is the flat rate, nil on property held past five years. Revenue 39.5% of GDP is the OECD Revenue Statistics figure. Debt ~26% of GDP (Eurostat, 2024) -- the lightest in this register after Luxembourg's. The spending split is the V1.2a policy split, not a reconciliation of the accounts.
